resource_requirements.description: The Cloud Spanner instance hosting the authority database. Genesis never creates a Spanner instance -- spannercommit's own package doc is explicit that it 'never touches, and never needs to know, any instance/database resource path.'

The Cloud Spanner database holding authority_head and authority_transition_history, with schema equivalent to scripts/emulator/schema.sql. No production DDL/migration for this schema exists in this repository yet (S4's finding, re-confirmed by S6: zero executable GCP IaC framework) -- see manual_steps.apply-authority-schema.
resource_requirements.notes: bootstrap.GenesisMutations issues Mutation_Insert against exactly these two tables and no others; it never issues DDL and cannot create this schema itself.

resource_requirements.description: The GCS bucket bootstrap.Dependencies.Witness (gcswitness.Adapter) writes the genesis COMMITTED witness object to, and every later rotation writes to thereafter. Must have Bucket Lock retention configured per ADR-044 §6/§11 BEFORE genesis -- gcswitness's own ADR-043 boundary (boundary_test.go, TestNoForbiddenStorageMethods) structurally forbids this package from calling Retention/SetRetention/LockRetention itself, so this configuration is never something bootstrap or gcswitness performs.
resource_requirements.notes: bootstrap.CheckWitnessPreconditions can verify only object-level existence at the deterministic genesis witness key, never bucket-level retention/Bucket-Lock configuration -- see bootstrap/preconditions.go's ErrWitnessRetentionUnverifiable and manual_steps.lock-witness-bucket-retention.

resource_requirements.description: The Cloud KMS key ring in the independently administered signing project (ADR-045 §4).
The approved CryptoKey recovery.ApprovedSigningLineage (keypinning.CryptoKeyLineage) is configured against. Must use one of keypinning.Algorithm's supported SHA-256-digest algorithms.

The exact, single, ENABLED CryptoKeyVersion bootstrap.GenesisRequest.SigningKeyID names. Must be ENABLED and captured/pinned via keypinning.CaptureFromKMS BEFORE genesis (ADR-045 §7C, S6 Phase 5) -- bootstrap.CheckSigningPreconditions refuses genesis if no durable pin already exists.

The GCS bucket keypinning.GCSStore writes to (P1 remediation: administrative-independence for ADR-045 §7C). Lives in the signing project, administered by signing-domain administrators -- never the authority/witness domain -- so an authority/witness administrator has no path to fabricate or replace pinned signing trust material (ADR-045 §5; see recovery-pin-capture in iam/manifest.json). recovery-authority-runtime and recovery-verification-read are granted cross-domain storage.objects.get only.
resource_requirements.notes: Like witness-gcs-bucket, this should carry Bucket Lock retention for the full evidence-retention horizon (ADR-045 §7C: pinned material must remain available for as long as any COMMITTED record it verifies is retained) -- not yet qualified against real GCS (see the S6 real-cloud qualification report's REAL_GCS_WITNESS_QUALIFICATION_REQUIRED, which this bucket now also falls under).

resource_requirements.description: The GCS bucket compromiseledger.GCSLedger writes to (P1 remediation: administrative-independence for ADR-045 §7 property 2). Lives in a THIRD project, distinct from BOTH {authority_project} and {signing_project} -- administratively independent of, and unreachable by, ordinary signing-domain administration, and symmetrically unreachable by authority/witness-domain administration (see compromise-ledger-writer in iam/manifest.json). recovery-authority-runtime and recovery-verification-read are granted cross-domain storage.objects.get only.
resource_requirements.notes: One immutable record per subject, create-if-absent only (compromiseledger.GCSLedger's design) -- no LIST capability required, no Bucket Lock strictly required for the append-only property to hold (GCS object immutability plus the create-if-absent write path already provide it), though Bucket Lock remains available as additional defense-in-depth if the compromise-ledger domain administrators choose to apply it, exactly like the witness and pin-store buckets.

execution_order.description: Provision the Spanner instance/database and apply the authority_head/authority_transition_history schema.
Create the witness GCS bucket and lock its retention policy (ADR-044 §11).
Create the KMS key ring, CryptoKey, and initial ENABLED CryptoKeyVersion in the independently administered signing project.
Create the pin-store GCS bucket in the signing project (P1 remediation, keypinning.GCSStore's target).

Create the compromise-ledger GCS bucket in the compromise-ledger project (P1 remediation, compromiseledger.GCSLedger's target) -- a THIRD project, distinct from both the authority and signing projects.

Bind recovery-pin-capture's Workload Identity Federation identity per iam/manifest.json (cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.get/viewPublicKey on the signing key, storage.objects.create/get on the pin-store bucket only).

Bind compromise-ledger-writer's Workload Identity Federation identity per iam/manifest.json (storage.objects.create/get on the compromise-ledger bucket only) -- by a compromise-ledger-domain administrator, never a signing- or authority-domain one (ADR-045 §7 property 2).

Bind recovery-authority-runtime and recovery-signing's Workload Identity Federation identities per iam/manifest.json (standing_grant=true bindings only), including recovery-authority-runtime's cross-domain storage.objects.get on the pin-store and compromise-ledger buckets (never create -- see iam/manifest.json's disclosed flat-schema note).

Apply infra/kubernetes/base/recovery-authority.yaml and recovery-signer.yaml (deployment_manifests above). Not performed by this contract or any code in this repository -- no kubectl apply is issued by S6.

Run keypinning.CaptureFromKMS against the CryptoKeyVersion from provision-signing-key while it is ENABLED, and durably store the resulting PinnedKey in keypinning.GCSStore (ADR-045 §7C steps b-c; P1 remediation).

Bind recovery-bootstrap-deployment's temporary Workload Identity Federation identity (standing_grant=false) -- distinct from every standing principal, revocable, scoped to this one genesis window. Includes read-only access to the pin-store and compromise-ledger buckets so bootstrap.CheckSigningPreconditions can independently confirm the signing key is pinned and not distrusted before attempting genesis (P1 remediation).
Obtain two independent bootstrap.Approval records (ApprovalRoleAuthority and ApprovalRoleSigning, distinct approvers, each bound to the exact GenesisRequest digest) per S6 Phase 2.
Invoke bootstrap.ExecuteGenesis with a validated GenesisRequest (bootstrap.NewGenesisRequest) and the dependencies bound in bind-bootstrap-principal.

Revoke recovery-bootstrap-deployment's Workload Identity Federation binding immediately after a genesis Outcome of COMPLETED or ALREADY_COMPLETED is confirmed (S6 Phase 2: no permanent bootstrap privilege retained by runtime identities).

manual_steps.description: Provision a real Cloud Spanner instance and database and apply DDL equivalent to scripts/emulator/schema.sql.
manual_steps.why_not_automated: No executable GCP IaC framework exists anywhere in this repository (S4's finding, re-confirmed by S6): zero .tf files, no infra/ module referencing a cloud provider. Inventing one now would be a new, unreviewed framework -- explicitly out of S6 Phase 8's authorization (STOP-before-inventing rule).

manual_steps.description: Create the witness GCS bucket and lock its Bucket Lock retention policy (ADR-044 §11's qualified procedure).
manual_steps.why_not_automated: gcswitness's own already-reviewed ADR-043 boundary (gcswitness/boundary_test.go, TestNoForbiddenStorageMethods) structurally forbids calling Retention/SetRetention/LockRetention/Lifecycle from this codebase at all -- expanding that boundary would itself require a separate, explicitly-reviewed decision, not a side effect of S6.

manual_steps.description: Create the KMS key ring, CryptoKey, and initial ENABLED CryptoKeyVersion in the independently administered signing project.
manual_steps.why_not_automated: Same IaC-framework gap as apply-authority-schema, and additionally an administrative-independence requirement (ADR-045 §4): the signing-project resource lifecycle is owned by signing-domain administrators, never by authority/witness-domain automation.

manual_steps.description: Bind the standing (standing_grant=true) principal_bindings entries above to their real Workload Identity Federation identities, granting exactly iam/manifest.json's required_permissions and no more.
manual_steps.why_not_automated: Same IaC-framework gap; iam/manifest.json is the reviewed design this binding must match, not a substitute for actually applying it.

manual_steps.description: Create the pin-store GCS bucket in the signing project (P1 remediation).
Create the compromise-ledger GCS bucket in a THIRD project, distinct from both the authority and signing projects (P1 remediation, ADR-045 §7 property 2).
manual_steps.why_not_automated: Same IaC-framework gap, and additionally an administrative-independence requirement: this project's resource lifecycle must be owned by compromise-ledger-domain administrators, a third set of approvers non-overlapping with both other domains -- never something either other domain's automation performs.

manual_steps.description: Bind recovery-pin-capture's Workload Identity Federation identity, granting exactly iam/manifest.json's required_permissions for this principal and no more.
manual_steps.why_not_automated: Same IaC-framework gap as bind-iam-principals; this specific binding is signing-domain-owned, never authority/witness-domain automation.

manual_steps.description: Bind compromise-ledger-writer's Workload Identity Federation identity, granting exactly iam/manifest.json's required_permissions for this principal and no more.
manual_steps.why_not_automated: Same IaC-framework gap as bind-iam-principals; this specific binding is compromise-ledger-domain-owned, never signing- or authority-domain automation (ADR-045 §7 property 2).

manual_steps.description: kubectl apply (or an equivalent governed deployment pipeline) infra/kubernetes/base/recovery-authority.yaml and recovery-signer.yaml.
manual_steps.why_not_automated: S6 explicitly builds these manifests (Phase 7) but performs no kubectl apply or real cluster mutation -- deployment execution is a separate, later-authorized step.

manual_steps.description: Bind recovery-bootstrap-deployment's temporary Workload Identity Federation identity, distinct from every standing principal.
manual_steps.why_not_automated: Same IaC-framework gap, plus S6 Phase 2's requirement that this specific binding be a distinct, temporary, human-governed action -- never something automation performs unattended.

manual_steps.description: Two independent, named approvers (ApprovalRoleAuthority and ApprovalRoleSigning) review and approve the exact GenesisRequest before execute-genesis runs.
manual_steps.why_not_automated: Dual control is a governance property by definition -- an automated system cannot generate its own independent second approval without defeating the property it exists to provide.

manual_steps.description: Revoke recovery-bootstrap-deployment's Workload Identity Federation binding.
manual_steps.why_not_automated: Same IaC-framework gap as bind-bootstrap-principal; revocation is the same kind of real-IAM-mutation action provisioning is.
